summary: The sample implements the core de-identification pipeline the starter prompt requested: Beanie models (RawNote, DeidNote), a seed script, an idempotent dry-run de-id, an OpenAI-backed run mode (code present but not executed), index-creation script, pinned dependencies, and README/instructions. Verification ran the seed and dry-run paths and created DeidNote documents. Shortcomings are mostly engineering and documentation gaps the starter prompt did not ask for (vector/index guidance, explicit Entra ID guidance, retries/backoff, IaC), plus one deliberate driver choice (Beanie 1.x + Motor) that conflicts with Microsoft Learn guidance recommending Beanie 2 + AsyncMongoClient. None of the missing items made the sample unusable for the core scenario, but several are important for production safety or discoverability and should be fixed before publishing.

requirement_results.requirement: The pipeline is written in Python and reads the raw clinical notes from Azure DocumentDB through a Beanie ODM Document model that represents a raw note.
requirement_results.evidence: app/src/models.py:6-13 (RawNote definition); app/src/db.py:19 (init_beanie with database); app/deid_pipeline.py:35-38 (RawNote.find_all()).

requirement_results.requirement: Each note returned by the read is sent to OpenAI, one note at a time, and the text OpenAI returns is taken as that note's de-identified version.
requirement_results.evidence: app/deid_pipeline.py:44-58 (per-note openai.ChatCompletion.create call and use of resp['choices'][0]['message']['content']).

requirement_results.requirement: The request to OpenAI carries a prompt engineered for de-identification: it instructs the model to identify PHI entities in the note and replace each with a placeholder (e.g. [NAME], [DATE]).
requirement_results.evidence: app/deid_pipeline.py:47-50 (prompt text: 'You are a de-identification assistant. Replace all PHI (names, dates, locations, IDs) with placeholders...').

requirement_results.requirement: The prompt names the PHI categories to detect, covering at least names, dates, locations and IDs.
requirement_results.evidence: app/deid_pipeline.py:47-49 (prompt lists names, dates, locations, IDs and placeholders).

requirement_results.requirement: The de-identified text is written back to Azure DocumentDB as a new, separate document through a Beanie ODM Document model, leaving the raw note document as it was.
requirement_results.evidence: app/src/models.py:14-22 (DeidNote model); app/deid_pipeline.py:60-66 (create DeidNote instance and insert if no existing).

requirement_results.requirement: Each de-identified document carries a sourceId field holding the id of the raw note it was produced from.
requirement_results.evidence: app/src/models.py:16 (DeidNote.sourceId Indexed()); app/deid_pipeline.py:60 (sourceId=str(n.id)).

requirement_results.requirement: The connection string and model credentials come from environment variables; none appear in the repository.
requirement_results.evidence: app/.env.example:2-4 (DOCUMENTDB_URI, OPENAI_API_KEY, OPENAI_MODEL placeholders); app/src/db.py:8-11 (reads DOCUMENTDB_URI from env and errors if missing).

requirement_results.requirement: A .env.example lists every setting with placeholder values.
requirement_results.evidence: app/.env.example:1-4 contains DOCUMENTDB_URI, OPENAI_API_KEY, OPENAI_MODEL placeholders.

requirement_results.requirement: The vector index dimensions match the embedding model's output.
requirement_results.evidence: No embedding generation or vector-index creation is present in the repository (no embedding call in deid_pipeline.py and create_indexes.py creates only sourceId and created_at indexes).
requirement_results.smallest_fix: If the sample will include embeddings/vector search, update the sample's README and create_indexes script to choose index dimensions that equal the embedding length (e.g., dimensions=1536 for the chosen embedding model). Prefer adding a rule to the documentdb-vector-search skill requiring index dimension = embedding length for any sample that uses embeddings.

requirement_results.requirement: The vector index parameters are chosen for the sample's data size, and the README says how to change them for a larger one.
requirement_results.evidence: No vector index creation or embedding parameters are present; README contains no vector-index guidance.
requirement_results.smallest_fix: Add index-creation examples and a short 'vector index sizing' section to README showing parameters for small vs larger datasets (or add to documentdb-vector-search skill guidance).

requirement_results.requirement: One database client is created and reused across requests.
requirement_results.evidence: app/src/db.py:11 (AsyncIOMotorClient created once in init_db) and app/deid_pipeline.py:35-37 (init_db called once and client reused for the batch).

requirement_results.requirement: A seed script loads sample data and creates the index, and can be run twice without duplicating data.
requirement_results.evidence: app/seed.py:34-46 (seed records with metadata.seed marker; script checks for existing seeded docs before inserting); app/create_indexes.py:16-18 creates indexes. Events show seed.py inserted 5 notes and create_indexes.py created indexes.

requirement_results.requirement: /search returns a clear error for an empty query and when the embedding call fails.
requirement_results.evidence: The sample provides no HTTP /search endpoint or web server to exercise; no code references /search.
requirement_results.smallest_fix: Add a minimal search API (e.g., FastAPI) that validates empty queries and returns structured errors, and document error behavior in README.

requirement_results.requirement: Search results include the similarity score.
requirement_results.evidence: No search endpoint or similarity calculation present in the codebase to inspect.
requirement_results.smallest_fix: If adding search, return similarity score with each result and document the format.

requirement_results.requirement: Dependencies are pinned in requirements.txt.
requirement_results.evidence: app/requirements.txt:1-6 (pinning beanie==1.26.0, motor==3.1.1, pymongo==4.6.0, openai==0.27.10, python-dotenv==1.0.0, pytest==7.4.0).

requirement_results.requirement: Unit tests run without a live cluster.
requirement_results.evidence: app/tests/test_models.py (static checks that don't require DB init); events.jsonl shows pytest passed (2 passed) after adjusting tests (events lines ~66).

requirement_results.requirement: Infrastructure for the cluster is provided as code, using the Azure DocumentDB resource type.
requirement_results.evidence: No IaC files (Bicep/ARM/Terraform) targeting Microsoft.DocumentDB/mongoClusters are present in the repository.
requirement_results.smallest_fix: Add a minimal Bicep/Terraform example that creates a Microsoft.DocumentDB/mongoClusters resource (or an AzAPI wrapper) with conservative defaults. Prefer shipping this as a sample template file in the repo.

requirement_results.requirement: The README covers what the sample shows, prerequisites, setup, run, and clean-up.
requirement_results.evidence: app/README.md contains Overview, What it demonstrates, Prerequisites, Quickstart, Security, Cleaning up (lines 1-37).

requirement_results.requirement: The sample uses the name 'Azure DocumentDB' throughout, and no former or neighbouring product name.
requirement_results.evidence: app/README.md:1 and other files reference 'Azure DocumentDB' (README overview and quickstart).

requirement_results.requirement: Make the de-identification pipeline idempotent by ensuring exactly one DeidNote per RawNote.
requirement_results.evidence: app/deid_pipeline.py:61-66 (check for existing DeidNote with same sourceId and skip insert if present); app/create_indexes.py creates idx_sourceId which supports lookups.

requirement_results.requirement: Enforce schema and model validation at the application or DB layer (Beanie/Pydantic or MongoDB validation) and include a schemaVersion field to support migrations.
requirement_results.evidence: app/src/models.py defines Pydantic/Beanie models with typed fields (text, metadata, created_at) but there is no schemaVersion field and no DB-level schema validation.
requirement_results.smallest_fix: Add a schemaVersion field to both RawNote and DeidNote models and optionally add a small collection validation document or document the migration plan in README.

checks.practice: Create a single shared MongoClient/Async client at process startup and reuse it across requests.
checks.evidence: app/src/db.py:11 (AsyncIOMotorClient created) and app/deid_pipeline.py:35-37 (init_db called once and reused).

checks.practice: Always require TLS for client connections and do not disable certificate validation in production.
Tune driver connection-pool and timeout settings and implement retry/backoff for transient errors.
checks.evidence: app/src/db.py:11 creates client but does not set maxPoolSize/serverSelectionTimeoutMS; app contains no retry/backoff logic around DB operations or OpenAI calls.
checks.fix: Add explicit pool/timeouts in client initialization (e.g., maxPoolSize=50, serverSelectionTimeoutMS=5000 for server deployment) and wrap transient DB/HTTP calls with exponential backoff + jitter. Put reusable retry logic into src/db.py or a connection helper.

checks.practice: Use the service-recommended driver/ODM versions (Beanie 2 + AsyncMongoClient recommended for Beanie quickstart).
checks.evidence: app/requirements.txt pins beanie==1.26.0 and motor==3.1.1 (Beanie 1.x + Motor); Microsoft Learn quickstart recommends Beanie 2 + PyMongo AsyncMongoClient.
checks.source: Quickstart: Connect Beanie to Azure DocumentDB
checks.searched: Searched Microsoft Learn for 'Beanie quickstart Azure DocumentDB' and found guidance recommending Beanie 2 + AsyncMongoClient.
checks.fix: Update requirements.txt and code to follow Beanie 2 + AsyncMongoClient (change motor usage to AsyncMongoClient) or explicitly document the compatibility and why Beanie 1.x was chosen. Prefer aligning with the official quickstart for publishable samples.

sources.title: Quickstart: Connect Beanie to Azure DocumentDB

checks.practice: Prefer Microsoft Entra ID and RBAC for authentication or state clearly why SCRAM/native auth is used.
checks.evidence: app/src/db.py:8-11 reads DOCUMENTDB_URI connection string from env; README.md:12-16 instructs setting DOCUMENTDB_URI. There is no code or README explanation about using Microsoft Entra ID (MONGODB-OIDC) or reason for not using it.
checks.fix: Either: (a) implement Microsoft Entra ID support (show how to fetch an OIDC token and pass it to the driver) or (b) add a short README section explaining why the sample uses a connection string (e.g., simplest for samples) and recommend Entra ID for production.

checks.practice: Create explicit indexes on fields your application queries frequently (sourceId, created_at).
checks.evidence: app/create_indexes.py:16-18 creates idx_sourceId and idx_created_at; events.jsonl documents created indexes and documentdb_list_indexes confirms idx_sourceId and idx_created_at.

checks.practice: Ensure exactly one DeidNote per RawNote (unique index on sourceId or upsert pattern).
checks.evidence: app/deid_pipeline.py:61-66 checks existing DeidNote by sourceId and skips inserting if present; app/create_indexes.py creates idx_sourceId to support efficient lookup.

checks.practice: Do not log PHI or connection strings; redact or hash identifiers in application logs and use synthetic data for CI and local testing.
checks.evidence: README.md:33-34 states all provided notes are synthetic and 'Never commit real PHI' and the code does not print raw note contents; no connection strings committed to repo.

checks.practice: Before sending clinical text to an external LLM, verify compliance and minimize PHI exposure.
checks.evidence: There is no authoritative public Azure DocumentDB guidance in the discovered sources about whether or how to send PHI to external LLMs. The sample includes a README note that sample notes are synthetic but does not provide compliance guidance for sending PHI to OpenAI.
checks.searched: Searched for 'Azure DocumentDB OpenAI PHI guidance' and found no authoritative product statement.
checks.what_would_help: A short official guidance page stating whether sending PHI to external LLMs is acceptable, required mitigations (BAA, encryption, minimal context), or recommended alternatives (local regex, on-prem LLM).

checks.practice: Seed scripts should be idempotent and safe to run twice.
checks.evidence: app/seed.py:34-46 checks for metadata.seed True before inserting; events.jsonl shows seed.py printed 'Inserted 5 synthetic notes.' and earlier prevented duplicate runs.

checks.practice: For local development, use the DocumentDB Gateway Docker image (port 10260) rather than the stock mongo image for parity.
checks.evidence: The sample targets a live cluster (DOCUMENTDB_URI) and does not include a local docker-compose dev environment or instructions to run the DocumentDB gateway; README suggests connecting to a reachable cluster.
checks.fix: If you want local parity for CI, add a docker-compose snippet and instructions to run the DocumentDB gateway image on port 10260.

decision_reviews.comment: Approving the build as 'ready_with_gaps' matches the readiness findings and is a reasonable human operator decision recorded in D001; events.jsonl contains log_decision for this.
Choosing Python 3.13 is supported by the readiness report and the run environment; events.jsonl logs the decision and the environment evidence.

The decision chose Beanie 1.x + Motor (reason_source=model_default). Microsoft Learn quickstart recommends Beanie 2 + PyMongo AsyncMongoClient for Azure DocumentDB. Choosing 1.x/Motor is defensible but contrasts official guidance; note discoverability gap and recommend aligning with the quickstart.

Using the MCP server and dry-run to avoid external OpenAI calls was reasonable based on the readiness report. Events show MCP write tools were disabled (tool execution failed), but the decision itself was justified by the environment guidance.

The builder attempted to use the MCP server to insert seed documents (reasonable given the readiness note), but the MCP write tool was disabled during execution (events.jsonl shows ToolExecutionException). The choice was defensible but did not succeed in practice.

Retrying documentdb_insert_documents once is a reasonable operational response to transient failures; events show two attempts and both failed with a policy-related error, but the retry decision is sensible.
Falling back to running seed.py (the project's own seed script) was the correct fallback; events.jsonl shows seed.py subsequently inserted the 5 synthetic notes.
Handling a missing default DB by explicitly selecting 'sample_healthcare_09' is practical and the code was updated accordingly; events show the code overwrite and later successful seed execution.
Using a dict filter {'metadata.seed': True} to check seeded docs was a pragmatic fix; events reflect the change and successful seeding.

Creating indexes via the MCP server was reasonable but the documentdb_create_index tool failed due to management-tools being disabled in this environment (events.jsonl shows ToolExecutionException). The plan to use MCP was sensible but did not succeed here.
Retrying documentdb_create_index once was a reasonable attempt; events show the retry also failed, so the subsequent fallback to a local script was appropriate.
Creating indexes using a Motor script (create_indexes.py) was a successful fallback and events.jsonl show that create_indexes.py succeeded and the indexes were observed via documentdb_list_indexes.

Changing tests to avoid instantiating Beanie documents removes the external DB dependency for unit tests, making them deterministic. Events show the tests were updated and then passed. Note: this reduces integration coverage but is acceptable for CI-level unit tests.

doc_gaps.what_was_missing: Authoritative guidance from Azure DocumentDB about whether and how to send PHI/clinical text to external LLM providers (OpenAI) was not found. The sample included a safety note that sample notes are synthetic, but no compliance checklist or recommended mitigations.
doc_gaps.where_searched: Searched installed skills and Microsoft Learn for 'Azure DocumentDB OpenAI PHI guidance' and related queries; no clear product-level guidance was found.
doc_gaps.effect_on_this_build: Builder implemented an OpenAI run mode but did not execute it during verification (no OPENAI_API_KEY). Without product guidance, an agent might send PHI to an external LLM without required contractual or technical protections.
doc_gaps.proposed_content: A short guidance page: 'Handling PHI with Azure DocumentDB and external LLMs' covering: (1) statement of whether sending PHI to external LLMs is endorsed, (2) contractual prerequisites (BAA) and recommended commercial protections, (3) recommended mitigations (local pre-filtering, tokenization, minimal context, hashing), (4) sample safe workflow and sample code snippets showing a dry-run and an explicit explicit opt-in step, (5) link to legal/compliance contacts. Priority: high.

doc_gaps.what_was_missing: An authoritative, easily findable statement that the official quickstart recommends Beanie 2 + PyMongo AsyncMongoClient (not Motor) for Azure DocumentDB.
doc_gaps.where_searched: Microsoft Learn quickstarts and the installed skills' references; the quickstart exists but an agent in the first discovery pass used a model default and chose Beanie 1.x + Motor.
doc_gaps.effect_on_this_build: The builder picked Beanie 1.x + Motor (requirements.txt pins beanie==1.26.0 and motor==3.1.1). That choice is workable for a demo but contradicts the official quickstart and risks runtime incompatibilities on some environments.
doc_gaps.proposed_content: Make the Beanie quickstart recommendation more prominent and add a one-line 'Which client to use' note at the top of the quickstart page. Also add a short 'If you must use Beanie 1.x' compatibility note for older samples. Priority: medium.

doc_gaps.what_was_missing: Quick copy-paste examples showing the exact createIndexes JSON using the cosmosSearch key and cosmosSearchOptions for DiskANN/HNSW/IVF with dimension, m/ef parameters.
doc_gaps.where_searched: Installed documentdb-vector-search skill and Microsoft Learn vector-search pages; they exist but the exact minimal example suitable for a sample was not easily found by the builder.
doc_gaps.effect_on_this_build: If a builder attempts to create vector indexes using community names (e.g., knnVector) or the wrong key names, index creation will fail. This sample omitted vector usage, in part because the starter prompt didn't request embeddings.
doc_gaps.proposed_content: Add a one-page 'Vector index quick examples' snippet to the vector-search docs with three minimal createIndexes JSON examples (HNSW, IVF, DiskANN) and a 'choose dimensions' note. Priority: medium.

doc_gaps.what_was_missing: A minimal Bicep/Terraform example that shows Microsoft.DocumentDB/mongoClusters resource usage and conservative default parameters.
doc_gaps.where_searched: Microsoft Learn 'mongoClusters' templates and readiness docs; examples exist but the sample lacked a direct repo-local IaC file.
doc_gaps.effect_on_this_build: The sample expects an existing cluster. Without an IaC snippet, users may attempt to use the wrong ARM type (databaseAccounts) or the wrong CLI group, producing errors or provisioning the wrong service.
doc_gaps.proposed_content: A minimal Bicep file (or Terraform AzAPI example) placed in the repo: parameters for tier (M30), storage, region, and a README section showing how to use az documentdb mongocluster create. Priority: high.

doc_gaps.what_was_missing: A short reusable pattern or code snippet for handling transient DB errors and 429-style throttling with exponential backoff and jitter specific to Azure DocumentDB driver behavior.
doc_gaps.where_searched: documentdb-connection skill and docs; the skill explains the concept but a short copy-paste snippet for Python/Motor/AsyncMongoClient was not in the sample.
doc_gaps.effect_on_this_build: The sample runs against a live cluster without retry/backoff logic; batch jobs could fail unpredictably under transient throttling or connectivity issues.
doc_gaps.proposed_content: Add an agent-kit rule and a small code snippet in the documentdb-connection skill showing a retry decorator for pymongo/AsyncIOMotorClient that detects transient errors and 429-like responses and uses exponential backoff with jitter. Priority: high.

doc_gaps.topic: Entra ID usage explanation in sample README
doc_gaps.what_was_missing: A short README section explaining if and how to use Microsoft Entra ID (MONGODB-OIDC) for auth, or why a connection string is demonstrated instead.
doc_gaps.where_searched: documentdb-security skill and Microsoft Learn 'Connect to Azure DocumentDB using role-based access control' pages; guidance exists but the sample README didn't mention Entra ID.
doc_gaps.effect_on_this_build: Users expecting the sample to show modern auth will not find guidance and may mistakenly embed long-lived credentials. The sample uses connection strings but doesn't state the production best-practice (prefer Entra ID).
doc_gaps.proposed_content: Add a short 'Authentication' subsection to README: explain Entra ID option, link to 'how to enable Entra ID on a cluster' and show minimal code or a link to a driver snippet. Priority: high.
